chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who acts by what Allah has obligated upon him, he is the most worshipping of the people.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of the most worshipping person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam Ali al-Murtada (AS) emphasizes that the foundation of piety lies in the faithful execution of obligatory duties (fara'id), a concept central to Shia jurisprudence. It underscores that true devotion is not merely ritualistic but is measured by the consistent adherence to divine commands, thereby distinguishing the most devout among believers.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who act by what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Obligated upon him, so he is the most worshipping one of the people’.
en.sarwar: 7. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’ alia ibn Muhammad from al- Washsha’ from ‘Asim ibn Humayd from abu Hamza from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following: “Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) has said, ‘
One who fulfills what Allah has made obligatory upon him, he, among the people, is the one who worships the most.’”
